I'm in the process of making my own robot, and would like to create a custom library for it.

I'd like to #include other libraries so I don't have to worry if they've been properly set up in the sketch, and use the functions available in them. I'll be needing to use the Wire library, and the Adafruit_PWMServoDriver library. One is a predefined library included in the Arduino software, and the other is a third party library residing in my My Documents/Arduino/Libraries folder. How can I include both of these from a custom library residing in My Documents/Arduino/Libraries?
How can I #include something other than "Arduino.h"?

(Based on using the arduino IDE in windows 10)

you can add Libraries to your sketch as follows

#include <Wire.h>
#include <RealTimeClockDS1307.h>

for custom library's you add them to

C:\Users\ (your user folder) \Documents\Arduino\libraries

or globally in

C:\Program Files (x86)\Arduino\libraries

.............................

in my example

"RealTimeClockDS1307.h" is in the RealTimeClockDS1307 folder in my user documents and "Wire.h" is in the global folder

Since you're asking, it's also worth pointing out the distinction between includes quoted with quotes and includes quoted with brackets.

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/21593/what-is-the-difference-between-include-filename-and-include-filename

So:

include <Wire.h>

include "MyLocalHeader.h"
